question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence ("Because every call ... fires and storms") in the text as a whole?

choices.text: It points out that operators took on duties beyond the connecting of calls.
It explains why switchboard operators were eventually replaced by automatic machines.
It questions whether a skilled operator could really work as quickly as the text claims.
It describes the equipment that operators used to link one line to another.

explanation:
**Choice A is correct.** After detailing the core job — connecting calls by hand — the underlined sentence widens the picture: operators "also became an informal directory service," locating doctors and relaying news.

**The Full Solution:**
- The first four sentences establish what the job officially was: answering, asking, and connecting lines with patch cords, at speed.
- The underlined sentence begins "Because every call passed through their hands," then adds the word "also" — a signal that a further, unofficial role is being introduced.
- Its function is therefore to extend the account of operators' work past the switchboard itself.

**Why the other choices are wrong:**
- B: The text never mentions automatic switching or the replacement of operators.
- C: The sentence adds to the account of operators' work; it casts no doubt on the speed claim that precedes it.
- D: The equipment — sockets, cranks, patch cords — is described earlier in the text, not in the underlined sentence.
passage: In the first decades of telephone service, a call did not go through on its own. A subscriber turned a crank, and a switchboard operator answered, asked for the destination, and connected the two lines by hand with a short cable called a patch cord. Operators sat shoulder to shoulder before tall panels of sockets, plugging and unplugging cords hundreds of times an hour. A skilled operator could complete a connection in a few seconds. __Because every call passed through their hands, operators also became an informal directory service, tracking down doctors after hours and passing along news of fires and storms.__

_meta.anchor: telephone switchboard operators — manual exchange work and informal community role

distractors.B: imports later history the text omits
